what: Quanta Services builds and maintains electricity and energy infrastructure. Its crews string transmission lines, build substations, connect renewable projects and lay pipelines across North America and Australia.
customers: Electric and gas utilities, renewable energy developers, data centre operators and pipeline companies.
money: transmission and distribution lines, substations and grid hardening
building solar, wind and battery projects
moat: Trained line crews are scarce, and utilities use a short list of contractors able to work safely on live high-voltage systems at scale.
risks: Margins are thin, about 4% of revenue, so cost overruns hurt
Work depends on utility capital budgets and regulatory approvals
Skilled labour shortages can cap how much work it can take
opportunities: Grid investment is rising sharply to connect data centres and renewable generation
Revenue has grown about 20% a year for three years and the backlog is at record levels
Owning its own training academies eases the labour constraint rivals face
watch: Total backlog and the book-to-bill ratio, plus margin in the Electric Power segment.
